title: ClickHouse scale-out: drain + re-add a shard replica (cluster-membership change)
description: The nexus-cli scale-out verb (add/remove a NODE -- horizontal). Exercises the per-cluster env's idempotent node toggles: scale-in shard1 to a single replica (remove ch-shard1-rep2 via enable_ch_shard1_rep2=false), confirm the shard still serves from rep1, then scale back out (re-add) and confirm the re-added replica re-syncs from Keeper. The full add-a-brand-new-node path (clone a VM + remote_servers + macros) is the same toggle plus a foundation MAC reservation; documented in handbook §1.A.5.

observe.what: terraform destroys the ch-shard1-rep2 module + its overlays (scale-in shard1 to 1 replica); shard1-rep1 keeps serving

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.44 "clickhouse-client --secure --host localhost --port 9440 --query 'SELECT count() FROM nexus.events_local'"

observe.what: shard1's data is still fully readable from the surviving replica (rep1) -- no data loss on scale-in
default -Vars (all enabled) re-clones ch-shard1-rep2 + re-runs its overlays (scale-out back to 2 replicas)

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.45 "clickhouse-client --secure --host localhost --port 9440 --query 'SELECT count() FROM nexus.events_local'"

observe.what: the re-added ch-shard1-rep2 re-syncs from Keeper + converges to the same count as rep1 (idempotent join)

whatProves: scale-out is a clean cluster-membership change: a replica can be drained (removed) and re-added idempotently, re-syncing via Keeper, with no data loss while the shard's other replica serves. The env's per-node enable_* toggles are the node add/remove primitive.
